title: Throughput entitlements, burn-rate model, and remediation framework for Dedicated
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Background: Enterprise customers on Redwood Dedicated require predictable token throughput and clear contractual remedies when committed throughput is not met. Existing materials focus on throughput SLA windows and simple crediting, but we lack an operationally actionable burn-rate model that ties observed capacity shortfalls to precise credit calculations, throttling behavior, and escalation steps. This ticket proposes a single integrated framework that defines: 1) a formal entitlement model (how throughput commitments translate to per-tenant capacity expectations), 2) burn-rate and windowing math for measuring violations, 3) a remediation/credit schedule with automated triggers, and 4) guidance for interaction with autoscaling/fleet controls so customers and support teams have consistent behavior and expectations.
goals: Define canonical entitlement units (tokens/sec per allocation, burst allowances, and smoothing) and how they map to contract language
Spec a burn-rate model: measurement windows, rolling averages, and exclusion rules for planned maintenance and customer-side errors
Design an automated remediation schedule: credit tiers, temporary throttles, and fallbacks, plus human escalation thresholds
Ensure model interoperates with autoscaling policies and fleet-level controls without surprising customers
Produce contract wording (legal-friendly) and an operator runbook for support and SRE teams
out_of_scope: Pricing changes unrelated to credit calculation
Implementation of autoscaler code (this ticket defines behavior; ENG tickets will implement)
proposal_summary: We recommend moving from a single-window SLA to a tiered burn-rate model: define a short window (1-minute) and long window (1-hour) measurement. Violations are computed using a rolling average of delivered throughput vs entitlement after excluding scheduled maintenance and customer-caused failures. Credits are computed on a graduated scale tied to percent shortfall and duration, capped per contract. Autoscaling interplay: when Dedicated autoscaler cannot restore capacity within a defined remediation window, platform automatically invokes fallback routing and initiates credits/escalation. Contract language will include clear definitions, observable metrics, and a customer-facing remediation timeline.
measurement_details: Entitlement unit: tokens/sec per reserved GPU pool mapped to a customer namespace
Short window: 1-minute rolling average; Long window: 60-minute rolling average
Violation condition: long-window deficit > 5% AND short-window deficit > 15% for >= 3 consecutive samples
Exclusions: scheduled maintenance (published >72h), customer-side throttles or malformed requests, and upstream provider outages documented in status page
Metrics to publish: delivered_tokens/sec, entitlement_tokens/sec, deficit_pct, windowed_burn_rate, affected_routes list
remediation_and_credits: Tier A (minor): 5-15% aggregate deficit for <1 hour -> automated 5% monthly usage credit cap
Tier B (moderate): 15-50% deficit sustained 1-4 hours -> prorated usage credit and optional operational rollback assistance
Tier C (severe): >50% deficit or >4 uninterrupted hours -> higher prorated credit + account manager SLO for remediation and extended remediation assistance
Credit computation: credit = min(contract_monthly_fee * deficit_weighted_duration / billing_window, contract_credit_cap)
Temporary throttles: when platform load exceeds safe execution thresholds, route new requests to compatible lower-tier model variants (if configured) and notify customer with reason codes
Customer-facing timeline: auto-notification within 10 minutes of detection, credit calculation posted within 48 hours, manual remediation/escalation window of 72 hours
autoscaling_and_fleet_controls: Autoscaler intent: prefer scale-up to meet entitlement; if node provisioning latency > configured threshold, trigger degraded-mode policy

Degraded-mode policy: enable controlled shedding (selective request rejection with 429+Retry-After and intelligible reason codes) or route to fallback model variant; must be documented in contract as potential temporary behavior
Rolling upgrades: must not count as entitlement violations if performed within maintenance windows and with traffic migration plan published
Fleet admission control: new customer traffic is admitted only if headroom >= entitlement + burst buffer
contract_language_notes: Define 'Delivered Throughput' and 'Committed Entitlement' precisely, including units and sampling method
Provide an explicit list of exclusions and the notice requirements for scheduled maintenance
Articulate customer remedies as a combination of usage credits and operational support; reserve right for platform fallback behaviors
Include a maximum aggregate credit cap per contract term and a requirement for customers to follow recommended best practices (client-side retries with jitter, backpressure handling)
Require use of certified fallbacks (model variants) if customer opts-in to fallback routing in contract
acceptance_criteria: PM doc with sample contract clauses and plain-language customer summary reviewed by Legal
Runbook for Ops/SRE with detection queries, alert thresholds, and escalation matrix reviewed and approved by SRE
Burn-rate math validated against historical Dedicated telemetry (small pilot run with 3 customers) showing expected credit calc within 5% of manual calc
Product sign-off that autoscaling interplay descriptions are implementable without breaking existing Dedicated contracts
Confluence doc published and linked to customer-facing contract appendix template
